newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon starts interrogation of Red Army suspects.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon starts interrogation of Red Army suspects.

text.p: A Beirut judge began on Saturday interrogating five alleged members of the Japanese Red Army charged with passport forgery and other offences carrying up to 10 years jail.

Investigative Judge Saeed Mirza started the session with Masao Adachi, one of the five suspects arrested in Lebanon on February 15. The others are Kozo Okamoto, Mariko Yamamoto, Kazuo Tohira and Haruo Wako.
Before interrogation began the five Japanese rejected two lawyers appointed to defend them by the lawyers union and appointed their own, Bshara Abu Saad.
Some 50 lawyers offered on Friday to defend the Japanese, saying this was an act of loyalty towards the guerrillas who had stood by Arabs in their struggle against Israel.
Japan originally hoped Lebanon would deport them to face trial in Japan on international charges but Lebanon announced it would try them for local offences.
